inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report (IFRS) cash-flow reconciliation share-based payment add-back RMB873.3m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp); equity-award tax withholding nil (A-share restricted-stock schemes are settled from repurchased treasury shares, no net-share settlement line).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted as at 31-Mar-2026 (Q1 FY2026 report): 7,603.3m issued A+H shares, less ~127m treasury shares (RMB9,741m treasury stock at the FY2025 average cost of ~RMB76.5/share), plus 48.9m potential shares from share schemes (FY2025 Note 12 diluted-EPS adjustment) = ~7,525m. Cross-check: Q1 FY2026 attributable profit 12,674.6m / diluted EPS 1.69 = ~7,500m. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; Midea is an active repurchaser (RMB11.7bn of buybacks in FY2025, 106m shares cancelled), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.fx_note: Model runs in CNY (RMB; IFRS statements in RMB'000). Converted to HKD at 1.1742 HKD per CNY, cross rate USDHKD 7.8472 / USDCNY 6.683 from Yahoo Finance at 2026-10-10 (CNYHKD=X printed 1.1721, HKDCNY=X 0.8513 -> 1.1747; all within 0.2%). Parity check against the Shenzhen A-share 000333.SZ: CNY 82.46 x 1.1742 = HK$96.82 versus the H-share's HK$93.65, i.e. H trades at a ~3% discount to A (it listed at ~20% discount in Sep-2024). Direction confirmed: quote = model x fx_rate. refresh_price.py does not move this rate; re-date it on any material CNY move.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are CNY, so the rate is built in CNY: China 10-year government bond ~1.85%, mature-market-plus-China ERP ~6.8%, beta ~0.95 for a global appliance/HVAC leader -> cost of equity ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5% to cover H-share/PRC capital-control and governance-structure risk. Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. Single WACC across scenarios: cyclicality, the China price war, tariffs and property exposure are charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path 0.35% of revenue ~= FY2025 'Related payments of lease liabilities' RMB1,587m (financing; covers principal and the RMB159m lease interest). Lease liabilities (RMB3,296m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct is D&A ex lease right-of-use depreciation: 9,339.7 total less 1,483.2 buildings+machinery ROU depreciation = 7,856.5 (1.71%); land-use-right and trademark ROU amortisation stays in D&A because those are bought, not leased.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted once in the bridge at FY2025 book value (RMB13,202.9m; NCI share of profit RMB575m = 1.3% of group profit, mainly KUKA and listed subsidiaries). Flows are consolidated 100%. Book is above a ~15x capitalisation of NCI profit (~RMB8.6bn), so this is the conservative side.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations. Midea is an operating manufacturer (appliances, HVAC, building tech, KUKA robotics); not a bank, REIT, LIC or holdco, so the routing table's 'operating company, non-US/cyclical' row applies. The captive finance company (loan receivables RMB12.4bn) is small and treated as operating. No prior memory entry: first valuation. ANCHOR CHOICE: the flows' year 1 is FY2026, so the cash bridge uses the audited 31-Dec-2025 IFRS balance sheet to avoid counting Q1 FY2026 cash generation twice; the Q1 FY2026 (31-Mar-2026, CAS) balance sheet is used for the share count and as a cross-check (gross liquidity ~RMB305bn, borrowings ~RMB54.9bn, net liquidity ~RMB250bn vs ~RMB237bn at Dec, the +RMB13bn consistent with Q1 FCF of 12.4bn plus deposit interest). The H1 FY2026 interim report (Aug-2026) is NOT in Extracted/; its headline figures in the Analysis JSON (revenue +3.5%, attributable profit +1.7-2%, ex-non-recurring profit -25%) informed the FY2026 driver year but were not verified against the filing. INTEREST: FY2025 'Other income' includes RMB8,444m interest on constant-return financial products (received in INVESTING cash flows, line 9277, so already outside reported FCF) and finance income RMB1,121m (of which RMB1,088m received in OPERATING cash flow). last_fcf therefore deducts only the RMB1,088m that sits inside OCF; the EBITDA anchor excludes all ~RMB9.6bn of interest-type income and RMB2,397m 'Other gains, net' (FX and fair-value gains). Matching assets are all in the bridge (cash, term deposits, constant-return products, FVTPL investments). EBITDA ANCHOR: FY2025 operating profit 54,743 - interest in other income 8,444 - other gains 2,397 + D&A 9,340 = 53,241; + SBC 873 = 54,114 adjusted (11.80% of revenue); FY2024 same build 48,231 (11.79%). FY0 tie: modelled EBIT ~44.0bn x (1-16.5%) + after-tax net interest ~4.9bn + associates 0.6bn + other gains after tax ~1.9bn - NCI 0.6bn = ~43.0bn vs reported attributable profit 43.9bn. WORKING CAPITAL: Midea runs structurally negative working capital (trade+note payables 130.8bn, contract liabilities 47.0bn and accruals ~110bn against receivables, contract assets and inventory of ~129.5bn), so wc_capture is POSITIVE (growth releases cash): 10% of the revenue increase vs ~15% observed in FY2025 and far more in FY2024. In a shrinking year the same capture runs in reverse. BUYBACKS: RMB11.7bn spent in FY2025; value-neutral in this model. BAND: SBC is ~0.2% of revenue, so house and street differ by only ~2% (base 123.9 vs 126.5 HKD). The price sits BELOW both, so the generated band_position (~-1,100%) is degenerate and carries no information; read it as 'the market is paying below even the fully-SBC-expensed value', not as a band location.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (16.0%) diverges >30% from revenue (9.9%) and EPS (10.2%) CAGRs because the Sep-2024 H-share IPO injected RMB32.2bn of new equity; ex-IPO the 3yr equity CAGR is ~10.2%. Revenue CAGR selected instead; it too is flattered by FY2025 acquisitions (Arbonia climate, Toshiba Elevator China, TEKA). The forward base path (4-5%) is deliberately well below it given the domestic downturn.
historical_growth.notes: Five-year IFRS summary in the FY2025 AR starts at FY2021, so 5yr CAGRs are null and 4yr (FY2021-FY2025) are given. Revenue 343,361 -> 458,502; attributable equity 142,932 (FY2022) / 124,865 (FY2021) -> 223,221. EPS 3yr uses FY2022 basic EPS RMB4.33 -> RMB5.80. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest received in OCF): FY2023 49,369, FY2024 50,646, FY2025 40,243; reported FCF 51,589 / 52,672 / 42,204. The two series move together because SBC is ~0.2-0.3% of revenue and most interest is received in investing activities; the FY2025 dip is capex stepping up (7.8bn -> 11.1bn) and a smaller working-capital release than FY2024's ~RMB20bn.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +4%: H1 FY2026 revenue +3.5% (Q1 +2.6%) with Carestream international consolidating from Dec-2025; domestic appliance retail forecast -6.7% (AVC) offset by overseas OBM (+16% in FY2025) and ToB (+17.5%). FY2027-29 recovers to ~5% on overseas and ToB mix, fading to 2.5% by year 9.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin 11.8% flat in FY2026 (Q1 FY2026 operating margin improved ~0.9pp YoY on lower selling/R&D spend, but Q1 AC retail value fell 13.8% and US tariffs persist), then +0.1pp/yr to 12.3% on ToB/OBM mix and the cost-leadership programme.
base.capex_rationale: Capex 2.4% (FY2025 2.43%, FY2024 1.92%, FY2023 1.69%) while overseas plants and robotics build out, easing to 2.0%; D&A ex lease ROU 1.71% rising toward capex as the asset base grows.
base.tax_rationale: Operating cash tax ~16.5% (P&L ETR 16.1%; many PRC subsidiaries on the 15% high-tech rate; tax paid 9.33bn includes ~25% tax on ~RMB9.6bn interest), rising to 17.5% as overseas mix grows and Pillar Two minimum tax bites.

scenario_narratives.base: Domestic white goods shrink in value through 2026-27 as trade-in subsidies fade and the air-conditioner price war with Xiaomi and Gree runs on, but Midea holds share and cost leadership while overseas own-brand sales (self-operated in 50 countries, OBM >45% of overseas Smart Home) and the ToB businesses (building tech, KUKA robotics, new energy, Carestream healthcare) carry group growth back to ~5%. Margin edges up ~0.5pp over five years on mix; tariffs are absorbed by the Egypt/Brazil/Thailand/Vietnam footprint. The RMB300bn liquidity pile stays on the balance sheet and is valued at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Overseas OBM and ToB both compound at high single digits: Arbonia, Toshiba Elevator and Carestream integrate cleanly, KUKA and the humanoid/embodied-AI programme commercialise in factory automation, and the domestic market stabilises after the subsidy hangover. Mix and cost leadership take adjusted EBITDA margin to 13%, toward global HVAC/building-tech peers, and an Annto logistics spin-off crystallises value without changing the operating flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: China's property slump and the post-subsidy appliance downturn (AVC -6.7% for 2026) turn into a two-year price war: revenue falls in FY2027, AC pricing (-13.8% retail value in Q1 FY2026) drags margin to ~10.5%, US tariffs of ~50% on Chinese appliances and steel-derivative duties squeeze export economics, and the RMB60bn three-year R&D push into robotics yields little. The H1 FY2026 25% fall in profit ex non-recurring items proves to be operating, not FX, and the ToB acquisitions dilute returns.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the domestic market is forecast to shrink in 2026, Q1/H1 FY2026 ex-non-recurring profit fell and tariff exposure is live; there is no solvency or refinancing risk (net cash ~RMB240bn), so it is not higher. Base 50% as the central path. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: overseas OBM, ToB acquisition integration and robotics commercialisation.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Midea is valued as a mature global appliance and HVAC manufacturer with a very large net-cash balance. The operating business is valued on owner FCF built from components (adjusted EBITDA ex all interest and FX/fair-value gains, less SBC, lease cost, cash tax, capex, plus the working-capital release that a negative-working-capital model earns on growth); the ~RMB300bn of cash, deposits and constant-return products is added separately at book, net of borrowings, NCI, the declared FY2025 final dividend and an operating-cash reserve. Because that cash pile is roughly a quarter of the market value, the result depends less on terminal assumptions than a typical DCF, and the H-share's discount to the A-share line is a separate, observable risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash pile quality: the bridge takes ~RMB216bn of deposits and constant-return products at book; part is pledged against note payables and part is effectively supplier-funded float that would unwind if revenue fell sharply.
Domestic price war and subsidy hangover: the AC price war and Xiaomi's share gains could push margins below the bear path.
Tariffs and geopolitics: US duties of ~50% on Chinese appliances, steel-derivative tariffs, German scrutiny of KUKA.

Earnings quality: H1 FY2026 profit ex non-recurring items fell ~25% while headline profit rose; this build reads it as mostly FX in the finance line (Q1 FY2026 operating margin rose), but the H1 filing has not been extracted to confirm.
Currency: flows in CNY, quote in HKD; a 5% CNY move shifts the HKD value by 5%, and the fx_rate is not refreshed automatically.
Terminal multiple: base caps the exit at 13x owner FCF against an observed ~11x EV/owner FCF today, so the base assumes modest re-rating; the bear's 11x is the no-re-rate reference.
